title: 'I'm honored to be your candidate': McCann thanks supporters at Kalamazoo gathering

 KALAMAZOO, Mich. — The energy inside the room began to settle down Tuesday night, but smiles and conversations continued as supporters gathered to watch election results come in and show their support for Congressional candidate Sean McCann (D - Kalamazoo).
 The Kalamazoo County Democratic Party brought together candidates, elected officials and supporters for an election night watch party Tuesday. 
 State Representatives Julie Rogers (D - MI) and Matt Longjohn (D - MI) addressed the crowd earlier in the evening, discussing their work in Lansing and the possibility of Democrats regaining a majority in the Michigan House.
 Jen Strebs also spoke to supporters, sharing her hope that they would be celebrating McCann’s election to Congress.
 McCann took the stage to thank the community, the party and the people who supported his campaign. 
 He acknowledged the uncertainty surrounding the results, telling the crowd he was feeling both nervous and encouraged.
 Election coverage: WATCH LIVE: Michigan Election Night coverage, results and analysis 
 “I think we’ll have a long night,” McCann said. “We’re not sure how the results are going to go, but I’m honored to be here tonight. I’m honored to be your candidate.”
 McCann has represented the greater Kalamazoo area in some capacity for 22 years. He said attending Western Michigan University was what first brought him to the community.
 “It’s been the privilege of a lifetime to be able to represent us and have a role in moving our community forward,” he said.
 McCann also took time to recognize several people who influenced his career in public service, including former U.S. Senator Carl Levin and former Congressman Howard Wolpe.
 McCann says his approach to public service has always centered on helping people rather than dividing them.
 “Public service for me has always been about helping others. It’s never been about dividing people,” he said. “It’s always been about problem solving and doing what I can to help regular, everyday people get ahead in life.”
 Republican candidate: Bill Huizenga emphasizes energy in final Election Day message to voters 
 According to McCann, his campaign has focused on issues including ending wars and suffering, improving prosperity and promoting the health and well-being of the community.
 While McCann hopes to have the opportunity to continue that work, he encouraged supporters to recognize the effort that went into the campaign regardless of the outcome.
 “I certainly hope it’s positive,” he said. “We should take the time right now to celebrate, to honor the effort of everyone here and those who aren’t, who have worked so hard to flip Michigan’s fourth.”
 Supporters continued mingling as the night went on, waiting for more results in a race with significant implications for the district and the future of Democratic leadership in Michigan and Washington.
